task.title: Monitor Connected Devices
task.shortdesc: Review the devices connected to the home network. Identify unknown or unauthorized devices and remove their access to the network.

prereq.p: Before you review the connected devices, make sure that:

ul.li: A computer or mobile device is connected to the .
You have the credentials for the .
You have permission to view and manage connected devices.
You can identify the computers, mobile devices, printers, smart home devices, and other devices that are authorized to use the network.

prereq.note: Do not block or remove a device until you confirm that the device is not authorized.

context.p: The displays devices that are connected to the home network. A device can connect through Ethernet, the primary Wi-Fi network, the guest network, an access point, or a mesh node.
Review the connected-device list regularly. This review helps identify unknown devices, unused devices, and unexpected connection activity.
context.note: A device can appear by a name that is different from its product name. Compare the displayed information with the network settings on the device.
Review device identity, connection type, assigned IP address, MAC address, connected access point, first-seen time, last-seen time, and traffic use when this information is available.

step.cmd: Create a list of authorized network devices.

info.p: Include the following information when available:
info.note: Do not include passwords, access tokens, account credentials, or other confidential values in the device list.

step.cmd: Open a supported web browser on the connected computer or mobile device.
Go to .
step.stepresult: The sign-in page for the opens.

step.cmd: Sign in to the .

substep.cmd: Enter in the user name field.
Enter the current administrator password.
Select Sign in.

step.cmd: Open the connected-device list.

info.p: The list can appear as Connected Devices, Client Devices, Device List, or Network Map.
info.note: Menu and control names can differ by .

step.cmd: Review each group of connected devices.

info.p: Review devices connected through:

ul.li: An isolated IoT network, if configured

info.note: A device that is not active can appear in an offline or previously connected device list.

step.cmd: Review the information for each connected device.

info.p: Review the following information when available:

ul.li: Connected access point or mesh node

info.note: Also review the device hostname, address-assignment method, first-seen time, last-seen time, traffic use, authentication method, and applicable access-control policy.

step.cmd: Compare the connected-device list with the authorized-device list.

info.p: Mark each device as authorized, unknown, inactive, or no longer required.
info.note: A device can use a private or randomized MAC address. Do not identify a device only by its MAC address.

step.cmd: Identify devices that have unclear names.

substep.cmd: Open the network settings on a known client device.
Compare the device name, IP address, and MAC address with the information on the .
Temporarily disconnect the known device from the network if its identity remains unclear.
Refresh the connected-device list and identify the entry that changes to an offline state.
Reconnect the known device.

info.note: Do not disconnect a device that provides an essential service or supports an active safety function.

step.stepresult: The known device is matched with its entry in the connected-device list.

step.cmd: Assign an identifiable name to each authorized device if the provides this function.

info.p: Use a name that identifies the device without exposing private information.
For example, use names such as:
info.note: Do not include a person's full name, password, telephone number, address, or other private information in a device label.

step.cmd: Investigate each unknown device.

substep.cmd: Compare the device name, IP address, and MAC address with the information for known devices.
Check whether the device is connected to or .
Check whether the device is an access point, mesh node, printer, television, camera, appliance, or IoT device.
Ask authorized users whether they recognize the device.
Confirm whether the device uses a private or randomized MAC address.

info.note: Do not block a device only because its displayed name is unfamiliar.

step.cmd: Review the activity of an unknown device.

info.p: Review the following information when available:

ul.li: Connected access point or mesh node

info.note: Do not use device activity information for a purpose that is not permitted by the applicable privacy policy or local requirements.

step.cmd: Block the device if you confirm that it is unauthorized.

substep.cmd: Select the unauthorized device.
Select Block, Deny, or the applicable access-control option.
Confirm the action.
Refresh the connected-device list.
Confirm that the unauthorized device is no longer connected.

info.note: Blocking a MAC address does not replace a password change. A device can use a different or randomized MAC address.

step.stepresult: The confirmed unauthorized device no longer has network access.

step.cmd: Change the Wi-Fi password if an unauthorized device used the primary Wi-Fi network.

info.p: Create a long and unique .
Reconnect each authorized device with the new password.
For more information, see .
info.note: A Wi-Fi password change disconnects devices that use the previous password.

step.cmd: Change the guest network password if an unauthorized device used .

info.p: Share the new guest password only with authorized visitors.
Disable the guest network when visitors do not require access.

step.cmd: Review the router administrator security.

info.p: Change the administrator password if an unauthorized person can have access to the current password.
Confirm that remote management is disabled when it is not required.
For more information, see .

step.cmd: Review the network access-control settings.

info.p: Review the following settings when available:
Remove rules that are no longer required. Confirm that each remaining rule has an approved purpose.
info.note: An incorrect access-control rule can block an authorized device or permit unintended network access.

step.cmd: Remove records for devices that are no longer authorized.

info.p: Remove saved entries, DHCP reservations, access-control rules, and device labels that are no longer required.
info.note: Before you remove a DHCP reservation or access-control rule, confirm that no active service depends on the assigned address or device identity.

step.cmd: Update the authorized-device record.

info.p: Record the following information:
info.note: Do not record passwords, access tokens, private keys, or other confidential credentials.

step.cmd: Verify that authorized devices can connect.

substep.cmd: Connect an authorized device to .
Confirm that the device appears on the .
Confirm that the device can access permitted local network resources.
Confirm that the device can access Internet services.
Connect a test device to if the guest network is enabled.
Confirm that the guest device cannot access the primary network or the .

step.stepresult: Authorized devices can use the permitted network services, and guest devices remain isolated from the primary network.

step.cmd: Sign out of the .

info.p: Close the browser if you used a shared computer or mobile device.

result.p: The connected-device list contains authorized devices. Confirmed unauthorized devices no longer have access to the home network.

ul.li: Regularly as part of network maintenance
After you change the primary or guest network password
After you add or remove a client device
After you add an access point or mesh node
After you configure a guest or IoT network
When you suspect unauthorized network access

postreq.p: If an unauthorized device reconnects after you block it, change the applicable network password and review the network security settings.
If you cannot identify or remove an unauthorized device, contact the through an approved support channel. For more information, go to .
postreq.note: Do not send Wi-Fi passwords, administrator passwords, account passwords, access tokens, or other confidential credentials to technical support.
